description:
#5057 — the two space CREATORS, both previously waived as "outside the single-space conformance snapshot scope". They are not: the snapshot projection excludes exactly one block, the harness's own test space (`FROM blocks WHERE id <> ?`), and filters nothing by space. A space is an ordinary top-level page row in `blocks`, and its `is_space` / `accent_color` writes are ordinary rows in `properties`. The fixture therefore needs no second-space TOKEN either: it CREATES the space it then writes into and names it `C1`, the same created-block convention every other arg uses.

What the single-space limit really was is the #891 SQL/Loro parity guard, which resolved every block against `TEST_SPACE_ID`'s engine doc. A space is not a member of itself — `ensure_test_space` leaves the harness space's `space_id` NULL and `create_space_inner` ends with `hydrate_space_block_into_own_engine` — so a created space was present in SQL and absent from the one doc the guard looked in, and the fixture failed on presence before any assertion ran. The guard now resolves each block's doc as `space_id`, or the block's own id when it is itself a space.

What the snapshot still cannot show is the space ASSIGNMENT: `create_page_in_space` writes `blocks.space_id`, a column the projection does not carry, and the mock's mirror `space` property is skipped on the TS side for exactly that reason. So it is pinned by its RETURN plus the page block it does put in the snapshot.

The mock divergence this found: `create_space` hardcoded `position: 0`, where the backend assigns a real sibling rank.

`move_blocks_to_space` IS pinned here, by the op below. Writing the `space` property routes through `apply_op_projected` → `hydrate_page_subtree_into_engine` → `projection::reproject_dense_positions`, which RE-RANKS the DESTINATION space's root sibling group — positions are dense per space, not across `parent_id = NULL`. `position` is in the snapshot, so that renumber is exactly what the fixture compares, and the mock diverged on it: the handler wrote the property row and stamped `blocks.space_id` but assigned no rank at all, leaving the arriving page on the rank it held in the space it left. (The retired waiver blamed `insertAtSlotAndRenumber(null, …)` re-flattening the cross-space group. This handler never called it.) The move is also observed on the READ path by the `list_all_pages_in_space` step: the seed page it takes out of the harness space stops being listed there. Two refusals ride along — an empty id list, and a target that is a live page but not a space.

Where the arriving page LANDS is the part worth stating, because it is first, not last. The engine orders a root group by each node's legacy `position` meta paired with its block id, and the two sides are on different scales: a node already in the space was seeded with the `position` it held at CREATION, which `create_block_in_tx` appended over the whole `parent_id IS NULL` set (every space and every page in one count, so it grows with the graph), while an ARRIVING node is seeded with its small per-space dense rank. The small key wins, so `Drafts` comes out at 1 and `inbox` — a space ranks in its own group — is pushed to 2. The mock mirrors THAT rule, not an append; the contrived cases it does not model are named at its call site.

What the harness cannot spell is the move's destination as a READ: a query step's args expand only `$SPACE` and `S<n>` (`expand_query_args`), never the `C<n>` label that names an op-created space, and query steps all run AFTER the ops, so there is no "before" leg either. The destination group is pinned by the snapshot instead, which is where `position` lives anyway.

`list_spaces` IS pinned here, by the query step below. What stood in the way was the two stacks' space BOOTSTRAPS, not their snapshots: `ensure_test_space` writes no `is_space` property, so `list_spaces_inner`'s `INNER JOIN block_properties ... key = 'is_space'` never sees the harness space, while the mock PREPENDED a hardcoded `Personal` row that no block backed. Only the mock half had to move. The prepend is gone and `seedBlocks` now lays `SPACE_PERSONAL` down as a real page block carrying `is_space = 'true'`, so the browser preview keeps its Personal row and the mock lists only block-backed spaces the way the backend does. That seed is irrelevant to this fixture — `clearMock` wipes it before the ops run — so both stacks enter with zero spaces and the only rows either can list are the two the `create_space` ops make. Their names are chosen so a locale compare and SQLite's BINARY collation order them differently — the ordering `SpaceSwitcher`'s `Ctrl+1`..`Ctrl+9` hotkeys ride.
name: spaces_lifecycle

ops.comment: A space is a top-level page block plus an `is_space = 'true'` property — no registry table of its own, which is why the snapshot carries all of it. `position` is where the mock was wrong: `None` means APPEND, and the seed already holds two top-level pages. The accent rides as a second property on the same block, and is `value_text` so the palette token survives verbatim.
ops.name: creates_a_page_block_and_flags_it

ops.comment: Into the space the op above made, named `C1`. The page BLOCK is in the snapshot; its membership is not — that is `blocks.space_id`, which the projection does not carry. The return is what names the block, and `parentId: null` makes it a root page rather than a child.
ops.name: creates_a_root_page_in_the_new_space

ops.comment: The SAME title in the SAME space. #4723: a live page title is unique per space, so this resolves to the page above and writes nothing — same id returned, no second block in the snapshot, no op in the digest. A mock that minted a fresh block answers a different label here.
ops.name: an_existing_title_resolves_instead_of_creating

ops.comment: A SECOND space, named so that the two collations disagree: `ORDER BY COALESCE(content,'') ASC` is SQLite BINARY, which puts `Work` (`W` = 0x57) before `inbox` (`i` = 0x69), while a locale compare puts `inbox` first. The query step below therefore reddens for a mock that sorts with `localeCompare`. No accent, so the row also shows the `LEFT JOIN` miss as a null.
ops.name: a_second_space_whose_name_discriminates_the_collations

ops.comment: The move: the seed page `S4`, rank 3 in the harness space, into the second created space. The `space` write is projected through `hydrate_page_subtree_into_engine`, which ends in `reproject_dense_positions` over the DESTINATION space's root group — `S4` comes out at rank 1 and pushes `inbox` itself to 2 (see the description for why the arrival sorts first). 3 → 1 is the renumber the mock had to start maintaining. The SOURCE group is not reprojected: the two remaining seed pages keep 1 and 2 with the vacated rank 3 left as a hole.
ops.name: moves_a_seed_page_into_the_second_space

ops.comment: `block_ids list cannot be empty`, refused before the tx opens: an empty selection is a caller error, not a zero-count no-op.
ops.name: an_empty_block_list_is_refused

ops.comment: `require_live_space_in_tx` runs ONCE, before any per-block write: `S1` is a live page carrying no `is_space = 'true'`, so the whole batch aborts. Per-block leniency covers a dead BLOCK id (skipped), never a bad TARGET.
ops.name: a_target_that_is_not_a_space_is_refused

queries.comment: The registry after the two `create_space` ops, with each row's name and accent riding as attributes because the id alone cannot see either property write. Two things are pinned. WHICH rows: `B6` (`Roadmap`) is a page IN a space and must not appear, and neither does `B4` (`Drafts`), the page the move put in one, and a mock that prepends a space no block backs answers a longer list. Their ORDER: `ORDER BY COALESCE(content,'') ASC, id ASC` is SQLite BINARY, so `Work` precedes `inbox`; a locale compare answers the other order.
queries.name: the_created_spaces_list_in_binary_collation_order

queries.comment: The harness space after the move, and the read half of the pin: `Drafts` was seeded into it and is gone, because `move_blocks_to_space` rewrote its membership. What remains is the two other seed pages plus the two `create_space` blocks — `create_space_inner` leaves a space's own `space_id` NULL, so the harness's post-op `assign_all_to_test_space` (and `stampMockSpace`, its mirror) defaults both into this space on BOTH stacks. The four titles are plain ASCII whose `COLLATE NOCASE` order and the mock's case-folded compare agree, so the step pins membership, not a collation.
queries.name: the_harness_space_no_longer_lists_the_moved_page
